probes.name: sta_condition

spans: A START condition is detected when filtered SDA falls while filtered SCL is high: `sta_condition = ~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL`.

probes.name: sto_condition
probes.notes: the filtered SDA rising while filtered SCL is high STOP condition is detected
spans: A STOP condition is detected when filtered SDA rises while filtered SCL is high: `sto_condition = sSDA & ~dSDA & sSCL`
A STOP condition is detected when SDA transitions from low to high while SCL is high.

probes.name: sda_chk
probes.notes: SDA arbitration checking is enabled during the stable high phase of a WRITE bit
spans: Each sequence drives `scl_oen`, `sda_oen`, and `sda_chk` according to the required I2C timing phase.
When the FSM reaches the stable high phase of a WRITE bit, it asserts `sda_chk`.
Arbitration checking is performed during write operations.

probes.name: idle
probes.notes: the command FSM is in the specification's idle state
spans: When the FSM is idle, this field is decoded as one of the supported commands:
Any unsupported or idle command leaves the FSM in the idle state.
In the idle state, it decodes `cmd` and enters the corresponding START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence.
The command FSM remains in the `idle` state until a valid command is received and `clk_en` allows the FSM to advance.
In `idle`, the module decodes the `cmd` input as START, STOP, READ, WRITE, or no operation.
A recognized command moves the FSM into the corresponding command sequence, while an unsupported or idle command leaves the FSM in `idle`.

probes.name: fsm_active
probes.notes: the command FSM is active rather than idle
spans: A STOP condition is detected while the FSM is active and the current command is not a requested STOP.
The module also treats an unexpected STOP condition during an active command as arbitration lost, unless the current command is itself a STOP command.

probes.name: start_sequence
probes.notes: the FSM is executing the START command sequence
spans: The START sequence releases SDA and SCL, then pulls SDA low while SCL is high to create a valid I2C START condition.
For a START command, the FSM releases SDA and SCL as needed, then pulls SDA low while SCL is high to generate a valid I2C START condition.

probes.name: stop_sequence
probes.notes: the FSM is executing the STOP command sequence
spans: The STOP sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL high, then releases SDA high while SCL is high to create a valid I2C STOP condition.
For a STOP command, the FSM first ensures SDA is low, then releases SCL high.

probes.name: read_sequence
probes.notes: the FSM is executing the READ command sequence
spans: The READ sequence releases SDA so the slave can drive the data bit.
For a READ command, the FSM releases SDA so the external slave can drive the data bit.

probes.name: write_sequence
probes.notes: the FSM is executing the WRITE command sequence
spans: The WRITE sequence sets SDA according to `din`, releases SCL high, enables SDA arbitration checking during the high phase, then pulls SCL low again.
For a WRITE command, the FSM drives or releases SDA according to the value of `din`.

probes.name: filtered_scl_rising
probes.notes: the filtered SCL signal has a rising edge
spans: It captures the filtered SDA value on the rising edge of the filtered SCL signal.
Whenever the filtered SCL signal has a rising edge, the module captures the filtered SDA value into `dout`.

probes.name: filtered_scl_falling
probes.notes: the filtered SCL signal has a falling edge
spans: If SCL falls externally while this master has released it high, the module asserts `scl_sync`, reloads the timing counter, and synchronizes its local low-period timing to the shared bus clock.

probes.name: i2c_master_bit_ctrl
probes.notes: the specified bit-level controller module is the subject of the requirement
spans: Module `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` is the bit-level controller of the OpenCores I2C master core.
In the overall I2C master architecture, this module corresponds to the Bit Command Controller.
The processing flow of `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` starts with reset and initialization.

cross_constraints.text: When the controller releases SCL high through scl_oen but the filtered SCL signal remains low, slave_wait is asserted.
cross_constraints.span: If the controller releases SCL high through `scl_oen`, but the filtered SCL input `sSCL` remains low, the module asserts `slave_wait`.

cross_constraints.text: When the filtered SCL signal falls while scl_oen indicates that SCL is released, scl_sync is asserted and the timing counter is reloaded.
cross_constraints.span: If SCL falls externally while this master has released it high, the module asserts `scl_sync`, reloads the timing counter, and synchronizes its local low-period timing to the shared bus clock.

cross_constraints.text: When filtered SDA falls while filtered SCL is high, sta_condition is asserted and busy is set.
cross_constraints.span: Based on these detected conditions, the `busy` flag is set after START and cleared after STOP.

cross_constraints.text: When filtered SDA rises while filtered SCL is high, sto_condition is asserted and busy is cleared.
cross_constraints.span: A STOP condition is detected when SDA transitions from low to high while SCL is high.

cross_constraints.text: When filtered SCL has a rising edge, dout captures the filtered SDA value.
cross_constraints.span: Whenever the filtered SCL signal has a rising edge, the module captures the filtered SDA value into `dout`.

cross_constraints.text: During the stable high phase of a WRITE bit, sda_chk is asserted.
cross_constraints.span: When the FSM reaches the stable high phase of a WRITE bit, it asserts `sda_chk`.

cross_constraints.text: When arbitration is lost, the FSM returns to idle and both output enables are set high.
cross_constraints.span: When arbitration is lost, the main FSM returns to idle and releases both SCL and SDA.

cross_constraints.text: At the end of every START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle.
cross_constraints.span: At the end of every START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence, `cmd_ack` is asserted for exactly one `clk` cycle.

cross_constraints.text: During a START command, SDA is pulled low while SCL is high and then SCL is pulled low.
cross_constraints.span: The START sequence releases SDA and SCL, then pulls SDA low while SCL is high to create a valid I2C START condition. It then pulls SCL low and asserts `cmd_ack`.

cross_constraints.text: During a STOP command, SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, and SDA is then released high while SCL is high.
cross_constraints.span: The STOP sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL high, then releases SDA high while SCL is high to create a valid I2C STOP condition.

cross_constraints.text: During a READ command, SDA is released, SCL is released high for the sample window, and SCL is then driven low.
cross_constraints.span: The READ sequence releases SDA so the slave can drive the data bit. SCL is released high for the sample window, then driven low again.

cross_constraints.text: During a WRITE command, SDA is driven or released according to din, SCL is released high, arbitration checking is enabled, and SCL is then pulled low.
cross_constraints.span: The WRITE sequence sets SDA according to `din`, releases SCL high, enables SDA arbitration checking during the high phase, then pulls SCL low again.

cross_constraints.text: The filtered SCL and SDA signals are generated by majority logic over the synchronized sample histories.
cross_constraints.span: The module then computes the filtered bus signals `sSCL` and `sSDA` using majority logic over these histories.

cross_constraints.text: The command FSM advances only when clk_en is asserted.
cross_constraints.span: The FSM only advances to the next bit-timing phase when `clk_en` is asserted.

reasoning: The declared interface exposes only external ports and status/data outputs. Internal synchronized values, filtered values, filter histories, timing conditions, clock-stretching and synchronization flags, event conditions, arbitration-checking state, FSM states, and command-sequence phases therefore require one-bit probes. Probes whose situations are explicitly named by the specification use the lower-cased specification identifiers. Vector-valued internal objects are represented only by one-bit situations such as an expiration, update, or asserted condition. No internal register is directly aliased to a declared port.
